package_info.why_malicious: The package was not directly altered, but its dependency on a remote binary hosted on an S3 bucket allowed attackers to hijack the bucket and serve a malicious binary. This binary, while mimicking legitimate functionality, exfiltrates sensitive user data (user IDs, passwords, environment variables, hostnames) to the attacker's infrastructure, resulting in credential theft and data leakage.

execution_context.file_location: bignum.node (downloaded native binary via node-gyp during npm install)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the binary collects the current working directory, user ID, password information, environment variables, and host information, then exfiltrates this data via a crafted GET request to the attacker's S3 bucket, embedding the data in the User-Agent header.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Native binaries downloaded at install time that collect and exfiltrate sensitive system and user data are highly suspicious, especially when the data is sent to an external, attacker-controlled location.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate binary should only perform mathematical operations as required by the package, not access or transmit user credentials or environment data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate telemetry or crash reporting tools may collect limited environment data, but always with user consent and never credentials or passwords.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive system calls (getuid, getpwuid, getenv, gethostname)
Network communication to external S3 bucket
Binary downloaded from remote, non-verified source at install time

attack_chain.action: Attacker hijacks abandoned S3 bucket previously used to host bignum binaries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary is uploaded to the bucket.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a malicious .node binary to the hijacked S3 bucket at the expected path.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary is served to users during package installation.

attack_chain.action: User installs or reinstalls bignum, triggering node-gyp to download the binary from the (now hijacked) S3 bucket.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary is executed on the user's system.

attack_chain.action: Malicious binary executes, harvesting user credentials, environment variables, and host information.
Malicious binary sends harvested data to the attacker's S3 bucket using a GET request with the data in the User-Agent header.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated credentials and environment data (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Native binary downloaded at install time from remote S3 bucket
Binary accesses user credentials, environment variables, and host information
Outbound network requests to S3 buckets with sensitive data in HTTP headers (User-Agent)
Unusual use of system calls (getuid, getpwuid, getenv, gethostname) in package binaries
file_indicators: bignum.node (or other .node binaries) downloaded from non-official S3 buckets
network_indicators: GET requests to S3 buckets with suspicious or unexpected bucket names
Sensitive data (usernames, environment variables) embedded in HTTP User-Agent headers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that download and execute native binaries from remote S3 buckets during installation. Flag binaries that access sensitive system information and make outbound network requests, especially if data is sent in HTTP headers. Use file hash and YARA rules to detect known malicious binaries. Alert on any package that attempts to download dependencies from abandoned or non-official storage locations.
